extracted.intended_audience: poets and creative writers looking for places to submit work, enter contests, find grants, and research publishers/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Locate and evaluate literary magazines, contests, presses, agents, and other venues that accept creative writing submissions; use Poets & Writers' databases and calendars to check policies, deadlines, fees, and fit before submitting. The page functions as a continually updated calendar and directory of submission and award opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest vetting / legitimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets & Writers carefully review the practices and policies of each contest before including it in the Writing Contests database; the database is described as 'the most trusted resource for legitimate writing contests available anywhere.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contests listed in this vetted database as more likely to be legitimate; rely on the organization's review of contest practices and policies when choosing where to enter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial policies (for literary magazines)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Literary Magazines database includes editorial policies—information about what the publication seeks and how it evaluates submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult a magazine's editorial policies to ensure your work aligns with its aesthetic and submission preferences before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Databases include submission guidelines for magazines, presses, and review outlets (e.g., how to format and send work, what to include).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow each venue's submission guidelines precisely; these are provided in the databases so you know length, format, simultaneous submission policies, and required materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Listings provide contact information for publications, presses, and agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use published contact information to address submissions correctly or to query editors/agents; the presence of clear contacts aids legitimate submissions and follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' tips and publisher-specific advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Small Presses and other databases include 'tips from the editors' and other editorial advice about what they look for and prefer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read and apply editors' tips when preparing submissions to increase fit — e.g., tone, themes, or manuscript presentation they prefer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent interests / fit with representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Literary Agents listings include details 'about the kinds of books they’re interested in representing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match your manuscript to agents' stated interests before querying; use the agents database to identify appropriate representation targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open reading periods / current_acceptance_windows
rubrics_metrics.description: An Open Reading Periods page lists all the literary magazines and small presses currently open for submissions; it is continually updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only when a venue is actively reading; check the Open Reading Periods list to identify publishers currently accepting work and to time submissions to open windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review Outlets database includes information about publishing schedules for outlets that run book reviews and similar content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult publishing schedules to time book review submissions and publicity efforts appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Databases (e.g., Review Outlets) include information about fees charged by venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of and budget for submission fees; use fee information to compare venues and to evaluate costs vs. benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and prizewinner history
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants & Awards and the Submission Calendar provide details about contest deadlines and past prizewinners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check deadlines carefully and review past winners to judge a contest’s aesthetic and competitiveness before entering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program eligibility and application details (grants, awards, mini-grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listings for programs like Readings & Workshops Mini-grants and the Maureen Egen Writers Exchange Award include information on who they support and how to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm eligibility criteria, required materials, and deadlines for awards and grants before preparing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of directories and event listings to find audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poets & Writers Directory and the Literary Events Calendar help writers connect with peers, find venues, and list/advertise readings and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain directory listings and post events to build networks and reach audiences; use the events calendar to find reading opportunities and audiences for your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Poets & Writers Guides and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject-based handbooks (Poets & Writers Guides) provide targeted information and advice from authors, agents, and editors on publicity, book deals, agents, MFA programs, and contests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these guides for deeper, topic-specific guidance when preparing submissions, queries, publicity plans, or applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and currency of listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources such as the Open Reading Periods page are described as 'continually updated' and the Submission Calendar shows monthly event and deadline listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on current listings for accurate submission windows and deadlines; revisit the calendar/databases frequently to catch newly opened opportunities.
